paragraphs.text: Tam is a gorgon , originally named Tamira by her creator Jace Beleren . Jace conceived of her as his perfect protégé, an ally who possessed his best qualities and was his equal in magecraft and telepathy. However, she grew into her own independent being, and sought a path forward outside of Jace's designs. When Jace died, he gifted her his planeswalker spark , making her the first attested Planeswalker to ignite after the Desparkening .

Tam has a slender figure, yellow-green scaled skin patterned with red and dark green stripes, and hair composed of tendrils that fade from white to red. Her tendrils levitate and writhe in response to stress. She has gold eyes that lack the petrifying glare most gorgons possess; instead, she can use telepathy to paralyze living things for as long as she looks at them. Her face resembles Jace's.

She is calm, composed, earnest, studious, and intense; a brainy intellectual who wields paradox magic to rewrite probability and potentially warp reality itself. She was created from Jace's best qualities; notably his cleverness and creativity. She is particularly fond of Ravnican coffee, on which she spends most of her university stipend. She knows some amount of Arcavian sign language.

Jace Beleren created her as a "backup plan" in case he died. After his death, Tam received Jace's spark and gained a deeper understanding of her feelings and wishes. Tam shares certain traits and personality characteristics with her creator.

Tam was artificially created by The Theorist, Jace Beleren , when the telepath severed a portion of his own thoughts and gave them form. The fact that his lover Vraska was also a gorgon may have been an influence on her species. Tam trained in the Theorix school of Hexhaven Academy as a telepath, with Jace as her mentor. He sent her to Strixhaven to spy for him and accomplish what he needed to do to get his reality set up, including kidnapping Jadzi , the Oracle of Arcavios, and pushing her through to the Echoverse . While in the Multiverse, she referred to Jace as her Teacher and didn't talk or think about him much to prevent mind-mages from catching a glimpse of him in her thoughts and starting to ask questions.

Soon after her creation, she witnessed Jace begin to undergo a transformation. Obsessed with his vision of a perfect Multiverse, he began to excise the aspects of his personality that dared to cause him doubt; first the selves that thought he couldn't, then the selves that thought he shouldn't. This disturbed Tam and made her begin to question if their plan could be realized.

Tam eventually left Hexhaven, returning to the Multiverse, and joined Strixhaven University around 4564 AR as part of the cross-planar student initiative, claiming to be from Shandalar . In her first year as a Strixhaven student, Tam signed up for an Introduction to Magibotanical Environments class, intending to move into the Quandrix College study track in their later years. Under the guidance of the teaching assistant, Dina , she visited Harrier's Wood, a forest some distance from the Strixhaven campus, to collect flowers. However, the faerie planeswalker Oko appeared and lured Tam, along with her classmates Abigale , Kirol , and Sanar , through an Omenpath to Lorwyn-Shadowmoor .

Abigale and the other students realized that they had accidentally traveled to another plane. They emerged into a meadow containing a free-standing dolmen gate, which, paradoxically, opened into a cave on the other side. Inside, they found carvings depicting a pair of large, winged, six-armed creatures. One creature had a moon for its head; the other, a sun. They found the moon-headed creature, the elemental Isilu , in a chamber beyond the carvings and accidentally woke it. As they fled back through the dolmen gate, waves of darkness radiated from the creature and flooded the world beyond, turning the day to night.

Fleeing from the creature, the students found their way back into the clearing where they had started, where they spotted a patch of daylight with a person in it. Upon approach, the kithkin asked them what they were doing, and realized that they were from another plane. She introduced herself as Brigid Baeli . She explained the nature of the plane, mentioning that she had come to see whether there was a link between the Omenpaths and the unusual strangers that had been arriving on the plane since the Phyrexian Invasion . As she spoke, the students watched the night wash over the Omenpath they had emerged from and erase it. Realizing that they would be there for some time, Tam asked Brigid if she knew anywhere they could stay, and the kithkin offered them hospitality.

Brigid brought the group to Goldmeadow , where they discussed their predicament. When Brigid heard that a faerie had been the reason for their arrival, she told them that they should seek audience with Maralen , queen of the faeries and a former companion of Brigid's. However, Isilu walked past the village, plunging a place that had been in Lorwyn for years into the darkness of Shadowmoor. Brigid told the students to escape before the xenophobic Shadowmoor kithkin attacked them, and they ran from the village, seeking Glen Elendra , Maralen's palace. When they arrived at the Wanderwine River , Abigale flew each of the others over, and they continued their journey. However, soon after they entered the Gilt-Leaf Wood , Kirol was kidnapped by an elven hunter, and none of the others noticed. When the three remaining students realized that Kirol had disappeared, Abigale turned back to look for them, but was startled by a large elemental and fell into a tributary of the Wanderwine.

Tam and Sanar decided to continue on Brigid's directions to Glen Elendra and arrived soon after, finding Maralen in crisis as she appeared to be turning into Oona . Because of this, Rhys , her aide, tried to kill her as he was sworn to do in such times, but Tam used probability magic to make him miss his attack and fall out a window. Maralen explained to the two students that she believed she was becoming Oona because of Isilu's premature awakening, and enlisted their help to prevent a disaster, promising them passage home in exchange. They fled with her to the Stinkdrinker boggart warren, where they found Ashling , an old companion of Maralen's. The four set out to track down Isilu, but they were halted by Brigid and the Shadowmoor kithkin.

As they were brought toward a kithkin doun to be imprisoned, an army of Lorwyn elves emerged to attack Isilu, and the kithkin joined them in battle to protect the night elemental. The students and Ashling fought the elves as well, but Maralen and Tam were injured with the deadly poison moonglow. However, Ajani Goldmane , who had been enlisted by the class's professor Liliana Vess to rescue the students, entered the fray with Kirol in tow, holding off the elves. Kirol had been forced by the elves' leader, Morcant , to pick dawnglow, a powerful medicine that could counter moonglow's effects. She had brought a vial into battle, planning to use it to kill Isilu and destroy Shadowmoor. Kirol, Sanar , and Kirol's new ally Lluwen snuck into the elven lines, stole the vial, and brought it back, saving Maralen and Tam's lives. Shortly afterward, Abigale returned, with Isilu's opposite Eirdu in tow. The two gods embraced, and balance was restored to the plane.

After this, the students accompanied Ajani through another Omenpath, going from Lorwyn-Shadowmoor to Shandalar and eventually back to Arcavios. At Tam's suggestion, Lluwen joined Strixhaven's cross-planar student program to escape the ruthless elven hierarchy of Lorwyn.
The following semester, Tam joined Quandrix College. She accompanied Lluwen to Titan's Grave to speak with Jadzi .

At Titan's Grave, the two endured the scrutiny of the strict professor Dellian Fel . Impelled to prove himself, Lluwen disrupted a ritual conducted by six Archaics , after which he and Tam witnessed the Dawning Archaic attack Titan's Grave and abduct Jadzi. Along with Ajani and her other friends, Tam was confronted by Chandra Nalaar , who believed that the disruption of the Archaics was due to the meddling of Jace Beleren . However, the Dawning Archaic returned, and in their efforts to fend it off, the students and planeswalkers fell into a chasm beneath Titan's Grave along with it.

Navigating the tunnels below the site, the students found the Dawning Archaic emitting waves of volatile, reality-warping magic, and Jadzi performing a ritual to calm it. While her friends were held back by the chaos, Tam used her magic to find a path through and approach Jadzi. Instead of joining the ritual, however, Tam pushed Jadzi into the nexus of wild magic and bade the others a tearful farewell before jumping into it herself. Both Tam and Jadzi disappeared, reforming in an alternate, warped version of Strixhaven .

Upon returning to the Echoverse, Tam settled back into her routine as Jace's foremost student. By this time, however, the Theorist had become an entirely different person, shaving aspects of himself away until only his most tyrannical impulses remained. Although she continued to help him develop the magical theory necessary to realize their plan, she harbored deep doubts about the viability of the plan — and, upon learning from the imprisoned Liliana that the Echoverse would need to supplant and destroy the original Multiverse, its righteousness as well. The Theorist sensed her doubts and sent her to Innistrad to take measurements and to see the worst horrors that the imperfect Multiverse had to offer.

On Innistrad, Tam spent some time at an inn run by a former cathar , who told her about the horrors of the Travails but explained that humanity persisted nevertheless. Later, she attempted to telepathically contact the monster that the innkeeper had told her lived in the moon . As she communed with the Eldrazi titan Emrakul , she attempted to understand her, but inadvertently betrayed knowledge of the Echoverse. Emrakul, a devourer of unstable planes, demanded that Tam lead her there, causing Tam to sever the link in terror.

Returning to Hexhaven, she was no more confident about the Theorist's plans. As she returned to his sanctum to confront him, she found several of his friends from before the creation of the Echoverse, who had tried and failed to reason with him. She conspired with Vraska to stop him, then left for Hexhaven's kitchen. There, she retrieved a raw leg of chicken, which she threw into Liliana's cell. The necromancer reanimated the chicken, freed herself, and killed her duplicate. Once Tam was confident that Liliana would try to stop Jace, she left the tower to try to help from there, but quickly realized that the Theorist had already begun his ritual as the original Arcavios loomed out of the sky. Hexhaven overlaid itself on Strixhaven first, and Tam scrambled through the chaos, trying to help the Arcavians. She ran into Kirol, and after quickly explaining herself, their reaction made her realize that the only place that could contain a solution was the echo of the Biblioplex. She desperately pushed her way through the throng.

Before she arrived, however, a mote of magical energy appeared out of the sky, falling into Tam and suddenly overwhelming her with magic. She remembered that there was another possible solution to the problem, and with greatly magnified telepathy called out again to Emrakul, telling her that there was a Multiverse which needed to be consumed. Back in her body, she looked up and watched Emrakul partition the two Multiverses, drawing the Echoverse into herself and consuming it. Searching for cover from the calamity overhead, she arrived at the Folioplex, where she found Kirol and her other friends. She explained herself to them and offered a new introduction, with no pretense. After they accepted, she promised to return to Strixhaven later, and her friends left the Echoverse through an Omenpath.

As she watched Emrakul finish, her attention was drawn once more to the magic that had touched her. As a familiar voice spoke in her mind, she realized that it was Jace's planeswalker spark . He had died and passed it on to her, along with a final psychic message asking her to continue his work and always try to make things better. Her being swelled with his knowledge and power, and the will to experience the Multiverse and make great discoveries of her own. She felt sadness at Jace's death, but also indifference, as he lived on in her. Tam, who had always struggled with the fear that she was a mere illusion, understood how real she truly was as she planeswalked away to Strixhaven.
Some time after the end of the Echoverse, Tam visited Vraska on Vryn , hoping for her help deciding what to do.
Tam's secret identity was spoiled in November 2025, a half year in advance, through a survey put out by Wizards of the Coast.
During design, Tam was initially named Petra.
